units.label: Real World (PERN/MERN storefront scenarios)
units.pins: UNGOVERNED in pins.js (no pin governs it), though node, react, typescript, zod, bcrypt, jose, react-hook-form list it in their tracks.
units.currency: real-world is in UNGOVERNED — the checker reports nothing for it. 17 pages bold **zod 4.4.3** (Zod latest 4.6.5).
units.notes: A cross-stack track: phases 0–8 (the app, database, node services, express API, react UI, JS functions, TypeScript, CSS recipes, MongoDB mirror). For each product its pages use, measure which version the code targets (spines, package.json snippets, imports) and compare to that product's current LTS/latest from endoflife.date / npm registry (curl -s https://registry.npmjs.org/<pkg>/latest). The question is: which versions do these scenarios apply up to, and does any scenario use an API that a supported line has since removed/deprecated (CONTRADICTED) or miss the now-idiomatic approach (MISSING/PARTIAL)? Keep the delta to changes that affect the scenarios' code.
units.syllabus_hint: No single official syllabus — use Full Stack Open (fullstackopen.com, University of Helsinki, free) and The Odin Project's Full Stack JavaScript path as the yardstick syllabus for a PERN/MERN app (auth, REST API, React UI, state, testing, deployment, TypeScript, CI). Our track is scenario-based (a storefront built across phases 0–8); map their topics against our scenarios.

units.label: DSA (data structures and algorithms)
units.pins: No pin — algorithms are version-agnostic; code examples are in one or more languages.
units.notes: The algorithms don't version, but the CODE does. Measure which language(s) and versions the examples are written in (grep code fences: ```js / ```ts / ```py / ```java; spines), then check each example language's modern idioms that the content should use or that make older idioms wrong: e.g. JS Array.prototype.toSorted/findLast/Object.groupBy/Map.groupBy/Set methods/structuredClone/at(), Python 3.12+ itertools.batched/pairwise/bisect key=/heapq max-heap functions in 3.14 (check), Java 21 SequencedCollection getFirst/getLast/reversed, record patterns in switch — take facts from the language's official docs only. DSA phase 2 closed; later phases in syllabus are PLANNED. Also check the interview-platform claims (LeetCode language versions, if the pages state them) — only if pages name versions.
units.syllabus_hint: Yardstick syllabus: Tech Interview Handbook's algorithms study plan (techinterviewhandbook.org/algorithms/study-cheatsheet) + the NeetCode roadmap topic list (neetcode.io/roadmap). Free: NeetCode (free videos), w3schools DSA (exists — check depth), VisuAlgo, CP-algorithms, Tech Interview Handbook, freeCodeCamp. Our track: phases 0–2 written (interview & practice, complexity, recursion/maths/bits); the rest is PLANNED.

units.label: System Design
units.currency: Not governed by pins.js. Phase 3 caching scaffolded, un-started.
units.notes: Concepts are version-agnostic, but pages name technologies (Redis, Postgres, Kafka, nginx, CDNs, HTTP/2/3, TLS 1.3, gRPC, Kubernetes…). Grep which products/protocols and versions the pages name or imply, and check each against its current supported line from endoflife.date / official docs: stale claims (e.g. 'Redis is single-threaded' without I/O threads nuance, HTTP/3 status, Kafka ZooKeeper removal in 4.0 / KRaft only, Kubernetes versions, Postgres features) are CONTRADICTED/PARTIAL. Unwritten syllabus items are PLANNED.
units.syllabus_hint: Yardstick syllabus: the free System Design Primer (github.com/donnemartin/system-design-primer — its TOC) + roadmap.sh/system-design. Free: System Design Primer, ByteByteGo's free newsletter archive/YouTube (the book is paid — say so), highscalability.com, AWS Builders' Library, the Tech Interview Handbook system design section. Our track: phases 0–3 (interview, method, request path, caching scaffolded).

units.label: Frontend Architecture
units.currency: Not governed — the checker reports nothing for it.
units.notes: Imported, 17 files: project structure, component architecture, state management decision tree, data layer, routing, styling, monorepo, env/config, auth… Grep every library/framework/tool it names or recommends and the version-era its advice assumes (e.g. CRA recommended? Next.js pages router as default? Redux as default? Lerna? styled-components status, Tailwind v3 vs v4 config, React Router v6 vs v7 framework mode, Turborepo/Nx versions) and check each against the current release/support status from official sources (endoflife.date, npm registry latest, project blogs — e.g. CRA deprecated Feb 2025, styled-components maintenance mode — verify). Grade stale recommendations CONTRADICTED; missing modern options MISSING.
units.syllabus_hint: Yardstick: patterns.dev (free — design, rendering, performance patterns), Bulletproof React (github.com/alan2207/bulletproof-react — project structure), roadmap.sh/frontend. Free: patterns.dev, Bulletproof React, web.dev. Imported track (17 files).
